clue.text: Admiring band's cool beat

parts.note: a fan is a cool, blowing device, read here as the noun
to club someone is to beat them

explanation.surface: A group of musicians has a laid-back rhythm that people admire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cool' looks like an adjective praising the band, but it is the device that cools you down, a FAN.

clue.text: Running water contains agents for beauty treatment

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
the CIA is the US agency of agents

explanation.surface: A salon uses flowing water with products in a beauty treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running water' is a river: the Fal, in Cornwall in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic treatment for the face is a standard beauty treatment.

clue.text: For example, Henry V, a giant stirring men

indicators.note: stirring means mixing up the letters

parts.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's King Henry V, a towering figure, rouses his troops.

explanation.definitionFit: Prince Henry of Portugal is known as the Navigator, so he is an example.

clue.text: It supports work Hannibal never started

parts.note: Hannibal Lecter is the serial killer of The Silence of the Lambs

indicators.note: started means only the first letter of never is used

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hannibal' suggests the general, but it is Hannibal Lecter of The Silence of the Lambs.

clue.text: Enable cub to move an inch

indicators.note: to move means the letters change position

explanation.surface: Help the young animal shift along a tiny distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inch' is not a measure: in Scotland an inch is a small island, and Benbecula is one in the Outer Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scottish place names an inch is an island, and this is a Hebridean island.

clue.text: Hot sausage? Cold and short, as far as one can see

parts.words: as far as one can see
parts.note: the horizon is the furthest line the eye can reach

explanation.surface: A shopper wonders whether the spicy sausage on view is cold and skimpy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts the last letter from HORIZON, leaving HORIZO.

clue.text: Hollow black blocks arrive

indicators.note: blocks means the black letter is lodged inside the arrive word

parts.note: to come is to arrive

explanation.surface: Dark obstacles turn up in an empty space.
explanation.walkthrough: A combe is a short valley in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A combe is a small valley or hollow in a hillside.

clue.text: In ring one caught feeble sound of champion

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: sound means we take a word spoken aloud and spell its sound differently

explanation.walkthrough: 'feeble sound' gives LYMP, which sounds like 'limp'. The definition is loose: of a champion at the Games.

clue.text: That's a name around Usk primarily

definitions.text: That's a name around Usk primarily

indicators.note: around means the other pieces surround the Usk letter

parts.note: IE (id est) means that is

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letter of Usk

clue.text: Succeeded in cycling out

explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeeded' looks like the verb meaning managed, but it is just the genealogical abbreviation; the definition is only the last word, as in workers who are out.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who have downed tools are said to be out.

clue.text: Latin employed when boxer needs minding?

definitions.text: Latin employed when boxer needs minding?

parts.words: Latin employed when boxer needs minding?
parts.note: a boxer is a breed of dog, so this is the Latin phrase on a sign warning visitors about a dog

explanation.surface: A pugilist's carer uses classical language when keeping an eye on him.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxer is not a fighter but the dog breed; the Latin is the Roman warning sign 'beware of the dog'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin words mean beware of the dog, written at Pompeii doorways and still on gates.

clue.text: Solver's put this at end of letter

definitions.meaning: addressing the person solving the puzzle, belonging to you

definitions.text: put this at end of letter
definitions.meaning: a sign-off before a signature, as in sincerely followed by the writer's name

clue.text: Old invader to hang after beheading

indicators.note: beheading means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: to dangle is to hang loosely

explanation.surface: An ancient raider is to be executed by hanging after his head is cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after beheading' removes the first letter of DANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angles were a Germanic people who invaded Britain after the Romans left.

clue.text: Watch batsman causing surprise

parts.note: to eye something is to watch it
an opener is a batsman who starts a cricket team's innings

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on the cricketer who is doing something astonishing.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the opener is one of the two batsmen who begin the innings.
explanation.definitionFit: A revelation that opens one's eyes is a startling surprise.

clue.text: Dude regularly in church in heavyweight anorak, ironically

parts.note: a ton is a heavy weight

indicators.note: the second in places the dude, in and church letters within the heavyweight and anorak words

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word Dude

explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd and 4th letters of Dude; the second 'in' then sets the whole run inside the other two pieces, just after their fourth letter. An anorak in British slang is a nerdy obsessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something insincerely or with mock seriousness is speaking ironically.

clue.text: Sewing mailbags, perhaps, for this crime

definitions.text: Sewing mailbags, perhaps, for this crime

parts.words: Sewing mailbags, perhaps, for this crime
parts.note: sewing mailbags was traditional work for British prisoners, a task done inside a jail

explanation.surface: A prisoner's work is linked to the offence that put him there.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase normally means a crime committed with help from within; here it is also literally a job done inside, British slang for in prison.

clue.text: Very little cash said to move around town

parts.note: to switch things is to swap them around

clue.text: Acceptable to stop wearing stockings made at home

parts.note: a quad is a quadrangle, a courtyard

clue.text: Favourite at palace taking lead …
